advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a drift test asserting `_INTERCEPTS` exactly matches the set of pure-intercept subcommands routed above `_dispatch`, so an added intercept omitted from the set fails CI.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:47-74 defines `_INTERCEPTS` as a literal set mirroring the ladder at lines 464-586
ABSENCE: search of tests/ for `_INTERCEPTS` returned no matches — nothing pins the set against the actual dispatch ladder

Pure intercepts (reconcile/review/verify-commit-ticket/...) have no help/*.txt (list of src/rebar/_cli/help/ shows none of these), so they are NOT covered by `known_subcommands()` and depend entirely on `_INTERCEPTS`
advisory.finding: `_INTERCEPTS` is a hand-maintained duplicate of the intercept ladder in `_main_dispatch` with no drift/sync test. A future pure intercept added to the ladder but omitted from `_INTERCEPTS` (and having no help/*.txt, so absent from `known_subcommands()`) would silently lose its central store mount, reproducing ad9f for that command with no test failure.
scenarios: A developer adds a new store-touching pure intercept to the dispatch ladder but forgets to add it to `_INTERCEPTS`

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `-h` cases (top-level `['-h']` and `['review-plan','-h']`) to the dd62 no-mount test loop so the `-h` guard branches are covered.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:90 `if sub in _NO_AUTO_MOUNT or sub in ("help", "--help", "-h"):`
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:92 `if "--help" in argv or "-h" in argv:`
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:605 dispatcher already special-cases `rest and rest[0] in ("--help", "-h")`
advisory.finding: The new `-h` short-flag branches of `_store_mount_eligible` are never exercised: the parametrized loop in test_help_and_unknown_subcommands_do_not_mount tests `[]`, `no-such-subcommand`, `help`, `--help`, and `review-plan --help`, but no case uses `-h` (neither top-level `['-h']` nor `['review-plan','-h']`). Lines 90 (`sub in ('help','--help','-h')`) and 92 (`'-h' in argv`) are thus untested; a regression dropping `-h` from either guard would leak a tracker and go undetected.
merged_from: The docstring/contract that a help token ANYWHERE in argv suppresses the mount (line 92: `'--help' in argv or '-h' in argv`) is only tested at argv position 1 (`review-plan --help`), which is already handled by the dispatcher's `rest[0] in ('--help','-h')` path. A mid/late-argv help token on a known subcommand (e.g. `['list', 'something', '--help']`) — the case line 92 exists to catch beyond position 1 — is untested, so a regression narrowing that check to only position 1 would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the loop tuple to include `["-h"]` and `["review-plan", "-h"]`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `_INTERCEPTS` stays consistent with the dispatcher's actual pure-intercept ladder (or a coverage note) so a store-touching intercept dropped from `_INTERCEPTS` is caught.
evidence: search for `_INTERCEPTS` in tests/ returned no matches
only test_verify_commit_ticket_auto_mounts_in_fresh_clone positively exercises one intercept's mount
advisory.finding: No test guards drift between `_INTERCEPTS` and the actual intercept ladder in `_main_dispatch`. The docstring states `_INTERCEPTS` mirrors the dispatcher's pure-intercept commands and that skipping the mount 'can never break a store-REQUIRING arm', but if a store-touching intercept is added to the dispatcher and omitted from `_INTERCEPTS`, `_store_mount_eligible` returns False for it and it silently stops auto-mounting — with no failing test. Only verify-commit-ticket (one intercept) is positively pinned.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict the help-token check in `_store_mount_eligible` to positional help (first token / `rest[0]`) so a `-h`/`--help` option VALUE cannot wrongly skip the mount for pure intercepts.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:92: `    if "--help" in argv or "-h" in argv:`
Dispatcher help detection is positional only: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:605 `    if rest and rest[0] in ("--help", "-h"):` and :596 `    if first in ("help", "--help", "-h"):`
verify_commit.py:187-195 returns exit 2 when `not os.path.isdir(tracker)` — the ad9f failure mode when the mount is skipped
verify_commit.py:154-169 `cli` does not call ensure_initialized; ABSENCE: grep of _llm_commands.py for `ensure_initialized` returned no matches, so pure intercepts rely solely on the central mount
dropped.finding: `_store_mount_eligible` skips the central store mount whenever `-h` or `--help` appears ANYWHERE in argv, but the dispatcher only treats those as help when they are the first token or `rest[0]`. A store-touching PURE INTERCEPT passed a `-h`/`--help` *option value* as a standalone argv element (e.g. `rebar verify-commit-ticket --message -h`) will skip the mount, then fail with exit 2 'ticket store not found' — the exact ad9f regression, because pure intercepts have no per-arm ensure_initialized fallback.
scenarios: `rebar verify-commit-ticket --message -h` in an attachable clone with the gate enabled
Any pure-intercept command taking an option value that is literally `-h` or `--help`
dropped.suggested_fix: Detect help the same way the dispatcher does: only treat `argv[1]` (or `argv[0]`) equal to `--help`/`-h`/`help` as a help request, e.g. `if len(argv) >= 2 and argv[1] in ("--help", "-h"): return False`, rather than scanning all of argv.
